newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply lower as stops hit.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply lower as stops hit.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended sharply lower Monday, after spot gold prices slid back below $350 an ounce, prompting execution of stop loss orders and renewed short selling, traders said.

"The breach of the $350 level in COMEX April gold means gold settled at its lowest level in about a month, leaving the recent uptrend shattered, and that is dragging the funds back in on the short side again," said Scott Meyers, an analyst with New York based COMEX clearing member Pioneer Futures.
COMEX April gold ended down $4.70 at $348.30 an ounce, the lowest close since February 20, after trading a $353.30-348.00 range. Estimated total gold futures volume was 60,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $347.50/00, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $351.40 and the New York close Friday around $352.00/50.
Gold prices had been drifting back in the past week, after a month-long recovery from three year lows around $336.00 which was driven by short covering by funds.
In data released Monday, COMEX gold open interest fell a further 2,862 lots Friday to 166,622 contracts, the lowest level since September last year, funds covered short positions, traders said.

The latest CFTC Commitments of Traders data, released late Friday, showed funds had reduced their near record net short positions in COMEX gold sharply in the past two weeks, and at March 3 were only net short 1,213 contracts.
Short term implied lease rates for gold have also fallen to their lowest level in months, below one percent, suggesting interest in shorting gold has fallen away, traders said.

But hourly and daily momentum oscillators were turning mildly negative again in the past few days, and popular moving-average trend-following indicators have signalled a reversal of the recent uptrend.

News Monday of the introduction to the Swiss parliament of a bill reducing the Swiss gold reserve requirement and allowing the Swiss central bank to carry out gold lending, was also bearish, traders said.

Under the Swiss constitution, the Swiss Nationnal Bank is mandated to hold gold reserves equivalent to about 40 percent of the currency in circulation, but the reform bill would lower the reserve requirement to 25 percent.
The bill, approved by the government, has still be passed by parliament and was based on a report made public by the Swiss National Bank and finance ministry officials last December.
Switzerland has about 2,600 tonnes of gold in its reserves.
Gold was weaker than silver Monday with the spot gold/silver ratio slipping to 66.8, after earlier recovering to 68.7 from 22 month low at 66.15.
COMEX May silver closed down 4.5 cents at $5.235, after trading a $5.290-5.230 range.
Gold was weaker than platinum also Monday, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread edging back up to $33.20 an ounce.
NYMEX April platinum ended down $2.40 at $381.50 an ounce, while NYMEX June palladium lost $3.85 to close at $150.00.
Russian palladium supplies are still seen lower than last year by many analysts, while demand for automotive emissions catalysts is seen rising.
